name: DBnomics Web API
summary: Keyless API that aggregates economic time series from hundreds of official providers (IMF, OECD, Eurostat, ECB, national statistics offices) under one uniform data model.
description: DBnomics mirrors datasets from statistical agencies and central banks and exposes them as providers, datasets and series with a common JSON layout. At check the providers endpoint reported 47,467 datasets and about 1.7 billion series. You can list providers and datasets, fetch one series or a filtered set by dimension values, run a full-text search across datasets and series, and list the latest updates. Each dataset keeps its original dimension codes and labels; each provider's own terms of use apply.

endpoints.summary: List data providers with their terms_of_use and website
List the datasets of one provider
Series of one dataset, optionally filtered by dimension values
Full-text search over datasets and series

license.name: Per provider: each provider's terms_of_use URL is listed in /providers

agent_notes: Start with /providers, then /datasets/{provider}, then /series/{provider}/{dataset}?dimensions={"country":["FR"]} (URL-encoded JSON) to filter. A series id is provider/dataset/series_code; the series_code shown in responses can carry an extra dimension suffix (e.g. USA.NGDP_RPCH.pcent_change) but the shorter prefix also resolved. Pass observations=1 to get period/value arrays, and metadata=0 to drop the large dimension label block. /search is slower (about 2 s at check).
caveats: Datasets are copies of provider data and can lag the original publisher; check indexed_at and the dataset's updated_at.
Responses without metadata=0 include every dimension label of the dataset and can be large.
Limit is capped at 1000 series per page; page with offset.
Observed an Access-Control-Allow-Origin of the request origin on one request and * on another; treat CORS as open.

verification.notes: Exact example request executed without a key; 200 with application/json.
